tools.use: Reveals marble-dust ink and can be set on a sconce. Not a weapon required by any boss.
Optional. Cracks a marked marble wall in the White Library.
Hookshot-like line. Optional fetches. Never the only walk.
Pushes or pulls a railed block one post from the tile Ellis can stand on. Required in the Iron Hayloft.
Swim permanent deep water. Never required in DG06.
Optional glide onto hay or a beam in the same room.
Optional blunt shot at a candle that can also be walked to.
Optional brace against the hayloft fan. The lever is the real stop.
Optional scoop. The reservoir's readable card reaches a dry notch without it.
Optional step between two panes in the witness benches.
Optional crack in the powder loft. Not a key.

mythology.setting: Addison County, Vermont only. No other county is entered.

protagonist.name: Ellis Perch
protagonist.rule: The same person continues in the next body. Each death advances fourteen years. Geometry does not.

marbleVein.role: Stores unrealized lives. The White Library is a county filing of that store, not the vein itself.

voices.voice: Treats the vein as a debt of unlived years and a crown as acknowledgment.
voices.otherVoice: Treats the same mythology as an office's excuse for calling a person a measurement error.
voices.rule: They interpret one mythology. They are not two religions and not a party of companions.

surveyor.role: An inherited human office that tries to eliminate uncertainty by perfect measurement, including entering zero where a life resumes without a birth.

integrationEvents.summary: When the Witness Without a Face adjourns and the playable record plus the docket contradiction are in hand, crown 2 (the Lantern Crown) is resolved. This is a proposal for a later integration. Nothing in this pack is a function the current runtime already exports.

crown1.note: Crown 1 is outside DG05–DG08. This pack must not be read as creating it.

eligibilityRuleProposed.proposedFormula: A later system may treat Embryonic God as eligible only when resolved crown count is at least 2, the Marble Vein has been acknowledged as holding unrealized lives, and both the Voice and the Other Voice have been recorded contradicting the Surveyor on the same event. This pack supplies crown 2 and the contradiction evidence dg08.ev.contradiction (the docket in Vergennes) plus the library and reservoir and hayloft as earlier contradictions. It does not flip a global eligibility bit and it does not define the function that would.

campaign.note: Links are proposals. Standalone entry grants the previous dungeon's goal flag without simulating that dungeon.

dungeons.name: The White Library
dungeons.site: The closed ledger annex under Merchant's Row, cut into the same white marble the county used for steps. Otter Creek falls are audible through the north wall and never shown.
dungeons.premise: Public shelves keep the births Middlebury was willing to claim. A second stack keeps the dates the clerks scratched out. Ink mixed with marble dust shows only under a lamp. Nothing in the stack asks Ellis to type, speak, or remember a word that is not physically present while it is being used.

input.keyboard: cardinal movement and a single action
input.touch: cardinal pad and tap on the interaction tile
input.parity: Every exit and interaction has a tile. No chord is keyboard-only.

campaignPrerequisites.note: The lamp is already Ellis's. This pack does not invent the dungeon that first hands it over.
Ellis has heard the Voice once at the Marble Vein. The Other Voice is not required yet.

proposedUnlocks.note: When the Erratum is bound, the Weybridge mill-race door (DG06) is the next proposed threshold. A standalone visit to DG06 may still assume this flag already granted.

death.epitaph: In {roomName}, the body stopped. Ellis Perch drew the next breath fourteen years on. The shelves did not add a year; the county will, if it notices.
death.voiceOnReentry: The vein kept the years you did not get to live. The library only files them.
death.otherVoiceOnReentry: Fourteen years is a clerk's habit, not a sacrament. The door is where you left it.
death.onReentrySolvedRooms: If a latch flag is set, the room is rebuilt in its solved pose. Half-moved shelves are not waiting to cage the next body.

shortcut.description: Once the sealed carrel has been solved, a return stair joins Index Hall directly to that carrel. A later body can skip the stacks, the stair, the mezzanine, the hand, and the ink aisle.

clues.text: With the lamp up, the north plaster gives three scratched dates in order, each with an arrow into a wheel: 1863, 1919, 1961. They stay on the wall while the wheels are turned.

Each wheel's frame is carved POSTED and currently shows 1849, 1905, or 1947. A footer cut into the sill reads SCRATCHED, NOT POSTED. The other face of each wheel is the scratched date already written on the plaster.
Lamp on the floor ink: UNLIVED BEFORE MEASURE, DEATH OPPOSITE BIRTH. The ink is under the lamp in this room and does not have to be memorized.
The ceiling beam is etched with the solved cross: west Birth, north Unlived, east Death, south Measure. End-carvings on the shelves match sockets of the same shape.
The doorframe is notched with the same walk as the uninked stones. Ellis can read the frame with a hand, without stepping on ink.
Under the lamp, uninked stones read KEEP and inked stones read STRIKE. The words sit on the stones themselves.
Three carved ticks on the desk show the beam: left, gap, right. The beam itself is visible when the lamp is on the sconce.
The desk blotter, under the lamp, shows circle then bar then wedge.

The blotter's wooden edge is notched with the same three signs, circle then bar then wedge, so the order is still in the room when the lamp is lowered. The covers themselves are carved with those signs.

evidence.name: Uncirculated card
evidence.text: A marble-backed card, letters cut, not inked: ERRATA — DO NOT CIRCULATE. Under it, smaller: births that resume are to be treated as corrections.

evidence.name: Two readings of one scratch
evidence.text: West bench, the Voice: What the county scratched out, the vein kept. Ellis is not a newcomer. Ellis is the remainder. East bench, the Other Voice: Or Ellis is a person the office cannot file, and the vein is a story told so the filing looks holy.

evidence.name: Margin of an unlived account
evidence.text: Account of Ellis Perch, unlived interval, filed beside the Bridport birth of 1849. Margin, lamp only: not an error. The public line still says the child of 1849 did not return.

evidence.name: Names the town reused
evidence.text: A shelf of name-slips with the second use scratched thin: same letters, a later body, a clerk's note that the first holder 'had already been counted.'

evidence.name: Survey rule four
evidence.text: Brass plate on the press: Rule 4. Where a life resumes without a birth, enter zero. A zero can be measured. A return cannot.

evidence.name: The bound erratum
evidence.text: The deleted line, restored in ordinary ink: Ellis Perch continues. The Surveyor's zero is crossed out. Neither voice signs it.

enemies.name: Paper moth
enemies.telegraph: Wings fold for one beat, then it steps one tile along the shared row or column.
enemies.lampNote: A raised lamp holds it one beat longer. The lamp is not required to kill it.

enemies.name: Ink blot
enemies.telegraph: The blot gathers, then slides one tile. It never crosses an uninked KEEP stone.

puzzles.reset: Each wheel cycles. A sill crank returns all three to the posted face. No combination damages Ellis or closes the south door.
playerTrace: Raise the lamp. Read 1863, 1919, 1961 on the plaster.
The north latch opens and stays open.

rooms.name: Ledger Stair
rooms.summary: The town seam behind the Merchant's Row notice board opens onto a white stair. A sconce and a scraped date teach the lamp without hiding the way on. This is the body-candle: death in the library returns Ellis here, fourteen years older, with keys kept.
solutionTrace: Enter from Merchant's Row onto the south stair.
Raise the lamp at the sconce if desired. The north stair is already open.
Go north into the public catalog.

rooms.name: Public Catalog
rooms.summary: Open marble shelves carry carved call numbers. The east wing is not a guess-locked gate; it is simply the long way around, used later only by the return stair from the index. A clerk bell here is a checkpoint mark inside the entrance room's death rule, not a second spawn.
solutionTrace: Read the carved ERRATA card on the west shelf.
Continue north. Nothing in this room must be solved.

rooms.name: The Scraped Dates
rooms.summary: Three marble wheels stand under a plaster wall. Each wheel has two faces: the posted county date and the scratched date. The lamp shows the scratched dates on the wall while Ellis turns the wheels. Wrong faces do nothing but click.
solutionTrace: Raise the lamp and read 1863, 1919, and 1961 on the plaster.
Cycle the wheels off the posted dates 1849, 1905, and 1947.
Leave north. The south door never closes.

rooms.name: Index Hall
rooms.summary: Four shelves ride a cross of niches: west, north, east, south. Their labels are carved, BIRTH, DEATH, UNLIVED, MEASURE. The beam shows the solved cross. The floor ink repeats it under the lamp. After the sealed carrel is solved, the east niche opens a return stair that skips the stacks.
solutionTrace: Read the beam: west Birth, north Unlived, east Death, south Measure.
Swap shelves with their neighbors until that cross is set. The crank undoes the work.
Go north. The east stair appears only on a later visit, after the carrel is solved.

The dust cache on the west jamb wants the optional dust key.

The gallery to the west is optional. The hammer crack to the east is optional and cannot be taken without the hammer.

rooms.name: The Erratum
rooms.summary: Boss room. The Erratum edits the aisle: it swaps shelves, drains light, then drops three lines. Ellis restores the carved sockets, relights two sconces, and breaks only the line with the cracked end. Defeat binds the page and sets the dungeon goal. The south door stays open so an unready body can leave.
solutionTrace: When the comma rises, put the four shelves back on their sockets. Strike three times while it holds.
Relight the two darkened sconces. Strike three times.
Break the line with the cracked end. Strike four times. Leave south if the body fails; the door does not lock.

dungeons.name: The Reservoir Without a Surface
dungeons.site: The disused lower race of a Weybridge mill on Otter Creek. The reservoir behind the race has a volume and refuses a surface.
dungeons.premise: A previous Surveyor, A. Vesper, tried to name the height of the water and drowned in the naming. The main walk is banks, catwalks, and a grate that opens only when the race is drained. Creek fins are never required to enter, finish, or leave. Deep water pushes a body without fins back to the nearest shore and deals no damage.

deepWaterPolicy.note: W never drains. = and ~ follow the race level. Water controls exist only in rooms whose floors are never deep.

input.keyboard: cardinal movement and a single action
input.touch: cardinal pad and tap on the interaction tile
input.parity: Every exit and interaction has a tile.

campaignPrerequisites.note: Proposed link from the White Library. Standalone testing grants it at the door.

proposedUnlocks.note: The Cornwall hayloft door is the proposed next threshold after Vesper is released.

death.epitaph: In {roomName}, the body stopped. Ellis Perch drew the next breath fourteen years on. The race kept the level Ellis last set. It did not keep Ellis in the basin.
death.voiceOnReentry: Vesper measured a surface and became part of the volume. Do not finish the measurement.
death.otherVoiceOnReentry: Vesper slipped. The office prefers a holier verb.
death.onReentrySolvedRooms: The ratchet, once pulled, stays pulled. An unsolved valve row resets.

shortcut.description: After the ratchet is pulled, the loft bridge joins the sluice hall to the penstock. A later body skips the gauge house, the flume, and the ratchet chamber.

finsShortcut.description: With fins, a current from the chapel reaches the landing and skips the long bank. The bank remains the walk.

clues.text: The staff on the wall has heights and no waterline. Cut beneath it: THE GAUGE IS A WISH. THE STONE IS THE FLOOR.

A wooden model of the race shows the flume grate open only when the painted water sits at the bottom mark. A plaque beside the cranks reads: LEAVE BY THE HATCH YOU RATCHET, THEN RETURN THE CREEK TO ITS STEP.
Three chips on the same model are turned open, shut, open. Ellis can walk back to this room from the valves.
A cloth already half off the valve faces shows chipped enamel: open, shut, open. Pulling the cloth the rest of the way does not change the order.
A bronze strip on the dry frame is stamped 2, 0, 1 under the words LEFT, MID, RIGHT.
Each weight wears the same numbers as the strip. The correct notch on each weight is cut deeper than the other notches.

evidence.name: Soaked field book
evidence.text: Vesper's crew, in pencil that survived the wet: Fins forbidden on the main sounding. A swimmer invents a surface by wanting one. We will walk the stone.

evidence.name: Plaque without a waterline
evidence.text: The painted gauge stops at numbers and never at a stain. Someone scrubbed the line off and did not paint it back.

evidence.name: Name on the long bank
evidence.text: Cut into the coping: A. VESPER, WEYBRIDGE. MEASURED AND WENT UNDER. No year of birth. A zero was started and left unfinished.

evidence.name: Chapel card
evidence.text: The creekfin chapel honors swimming and then forbids it for the office. Last line, Other Voice scratched under the Voice's blessing: The office is walked. The rest is weather.

evidence.name: Buoy card
evidence.text: A card the race pushes into the dry notch at every level: SURFACE: NONE. VOLUME: AS LAST LIED.

evidence.name: Unsounded scrap
evidence.text: A zinc tag on the ladder: this spring was left out of the model because it would not take a zero. Fins or no fins, it is not the way out of the dungeon.

evidence.name: Vesper's office nail
evidence.text: The nail the Surveyors pass. It is bent. It does not name a height.

enemies.name: Silt eel

dungeons.name: The Iron Hayloft
dungeons.site: A barn raised on iron posts above the intervale hay meadows, west of the Lemon Fair's low fog. The parish called the machinery a saint.
dungeons.premise: H. Pell's loft counts every stalk and forgets the eater. Counterweights, a block rod, and threshing iron do the counting. Blocks ride rails with end stops. Each block room has a crank the blocks cannot reach. Leaving a room unsolved restores the rails. No block can cover a door.

death.epitaph: In {roomName}, the body stopped. Ellis Perch drew the next breath fourteen years on. Unlatched weights went back to their first posts.
death.voiceOnReentry: The saint counted the stalk and not the mouth. You are the mouth.
death.otherVoiceOnReentry: It is a barn. The iron is heavy because iron is heavy.

shortcut.description: After the east mow is latched, a roof door in the nave opens onto the antechamber, skipping the mow, rope walk, choir, bridge, bailer, and east mow on a later body.

clues.text: A soot shadow on the north wall is the solved silhouette: left weight low, middle weight high, right weight in the middle hole.
The iron palm in the corner is a relief in that same pose. Three fingers: down, up, half. They are the weights.
The floor is painted with a pull arrow toward the west plate. The arrow starts at the block's far post.
An iron post fills the tile east of the far post. Ellis cannot stand behind the block. The rod is the pull. The crank west of the rail restores the far post.
The box lid is cut triangle, square, round. The stones are those shapes and will not sit in a foreign hole.
The rim repeats the cutouts left to right and adds the words AS THE LID, not as the tally.
The main plate is painted with a hay sheaf. A second plate further along is painted with a spare knot and opens only a niche.

evidence.name: Rod diagram
evidence.text: Burned into the lintel: a block, a hand, a hooked rod. Push is the hand. Pull is the rod. The practice rail under the lintel cannot reach the doors.

evidence.name: The palm's other reading
evidence.text: Under the relief, the Voice: The saint keeps the parish by measure. The Other Voice, scratched in the iron: The parish kept itself. Pell kept the count.

evidence.name: Farmhand slip
evidence.text: A slip nailed under the stair: Pell counts the grain and forgets the eater. If the loft locks you in, the crank is on the catwalk the weights are not allowed to use. Signed with a thumb, no surname.

evidence.name: Tally that will not close
evidence.text: Beside the shape box, a column of stalks ends in a blank. The blank is labeled EATER. Nothing in the loft is shaped to fill it.

evidence.name: The eaten, released
evidence.text: When the saint unbinds, the blank on the tally is no longer a problem to solve. The slip simply reads: the eaters were always in the intervale, uncounted, which is not the same as unreal.

dungeons.name: The Lantern Court
dungeons.site: A court annex off the falls that is only in session where lanterns have been set down. It is not City Hall. It convenes in the gap the city did not measure.
dungeons.premise: Shadows copy what Ellis just did. The copy is written on a testimony rail as verb and direction, eight beats visible, newest last. An exemplar performs the legal sequence in the room, and the same sequence is cut into stone or wood there. A clerk's bell rewinds the copy without taking keys. The Second Crown is resolved here as a proposed integration event. It does not grant Embryonic God.

input.keyboard: cardinal movement and a single action
input.touch: cardinal pad and tap on the interaction tile
input.parity: WAIT, PLACE, and RING are tiles, not keyboard-only chords.

campaignPrerequisites.note: Placed light uses the lamp plus spare court lanterns that never leave the room.

proposedUnlocks.note: Resolves crown 2, the Lantern Crown. Eligibility for Embryonic God is a contribution recorded in integration/second-crown.event.json. This pack does not set that eligibility.

death.epitaph: In {roomName}, the body stopped. Ellis Perch drew the next breath fourteen years on. The rail of that attempt is blank. The docket is not.
death.voiceOnReentry: The court finally kept a face for the unmeasured life. You did not lend it yours.
death.otherVoiceOnReentry: The court kept a record of a refusal. Do not let the office call the refusal a birth.

shortcut.description: After the playable record is latched, a service corridor joins the docket hall to the crown threshold. A later body skips the middle court.

clues.text: An exemplar shadow loops north, north, east, ring. It repeats until Ellis matches it or rings the bell.
The same four beats are inlaid in the floor in slate: N, N, E, a bell-cut.
The exemplar plays north, east, east, north, ring, and then plays it again.
The wall carving is the same five beats. The testimony rail shows Ellis's beats beside it, mismatch in red wax.
Arrows cut in Ellis's rail read north, north, south. The shadow's next tile is chalked before it moves.
The exemplar walks that arrow order on the far rail, forever, including the plates lighting as it goes.

evidence.name: The Town vs. The Unmeasured Life
evidence.text: Docket heading cut into the bench. The charge is that a life resumed in Addison County without a new birth, and that the office would like this called a zero.

evidence.name: The two voices on one event
evidence.text: Voice, left bench: The vein kept Ellis because a crown must be worn by a continued life. Other Voice, right bench: A continued life is a person. A crown is the court admitting it failed to file the person. They are answering the same docket line and do not agree.

evidence.name: Scrap under the bench
evidence.text: A juror's scrap: we copied the steps we were shown. When the copy went wrong the bell put us back at the start of the steps, not at the start of our lives.

evidence.name: Exhibit card
evidence.text: The card inside the cage, repeating the docket so it does not have to be remembered: nail, page, lantern. The bases of the three objects are stamped with those words.

evidence.name: The playable record
evidence.text: The floor keeps Ellis's successful five beats as a record that can be walked again. It is evidence because it was done, not because it was written about. The Second Crown proposal requires this record alongside the adjournment.

evidence.name: Scraped years
evidence.text: Portraits with the faces planed off. The lamp finds years, not mouths: 1849, 1863, 1877, and onward by fourteens. Optional. The court does not require Ellis to count them.

evidence.name: Adjournment
evidence.text: The witness without a face bows. The record states that Ellis stood where a face was asked for and set down a light instead. Crown two is marked resolved. No god is declared.

enemies.name: Shade clerk
enemies.telegraph: An afterimage flickers on the tile the clerk will step to, one beat later, copying Ellis's last cardinal step.

Go north. East is closed until the playable record exists.

rooms.name: The Witness Without a Face
rooms.summary: Boss. An empty face asks to be worn. Ellis places lanterns where the exemplar places them, reads the chalk copy before each lunge, and sets the lamp on the center stand instead of offering a face. The bell clears a bad copy and keeps the hit count already landed. Adjournment resolves the Second Crown as a proposal.
solutionTrace: Place lanterns left, right, and bench as the exemplar does. Strike the solid shadow three times.
Read the chalk. Step aside. Strike three times on the recovery. Ring the bell if the copy is garbage; the strikes already landed stay.
Set the lamp on the center stand. Strike four times. The crown event is proposed at adjournment, not before.

mirror.note: A banner over the aisle shows the direction the bailiff will copy next: Ellis's previous step. WAIT is a legal step.

stalled.tell: The banner reads WAIT. The bailiff copies it and does not move.

b_h0.note: The bailiff copied WAIT and stalled.

call_to_order.note: The docket board lights with the phase order and stays lit. South door stays open.

phase1_place.tell: An exemplar shadow places lanterns left, right, then bench, once, in view.

phase2_copy.tell: The witness stores three steps. Before any lunge, chalk draws those steps on the floor.

phase2_lunge.tell: The lunge follows the chalk and not a hidden buffer.

phase3_mask.tell: A mask walks. The docket line reads: the face is the light you put down.

adjourned.note: The witness bows to an empty bench. This is the proposed Second Crown resolution, not a costume and not Embryonic God by itself.

p1_h0.note: The witness's shadow is solid where the lanterns agree with the docket.

p2_h0.note: The lunge missed. The chalked copy is still on the floor.

p3_h0.note: The mask burns on the center stand. The face does not arrive.
